name: Lucca
title: Holidays in Lucca
intro: A Tuscan town ringed by tree-lined Renaissance walls you can cycle around, with towers, piazzas and Pisa just down the road. Here's what Lucca is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The oval Piazza dell'Anfiteatro in Lucca, lined with houses and cafés
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April to June and September to October are best, warm and green for cycling and day trips. July and August are hot. The Lucca Comics & Games festival takes over the town in late October or early November, and the Puccini festival runs in summer.

things.name: City walls
things.blurb: Walk or cycle the 4 km of tree-lined walls around the old town. Bikes are easy to hire.

things.name: Guinigi Tower
things.blurb: A medieval tower with oak trees growing on top.

things.name: Piazza dell'Anfiteatro
things.blurb: An oval square built on the shape of a Roman amphitheatre.

things.name: San Michele in Foro
things.blurb: A church with a tall, lacy white façade.

things.name: Pisa
things.blurb: The Leaning Tower, about 30 minutes away by train.

things.name: Garfagnana
things.blurb: Mountain villages and the medieval Devil's Bridge, an hour north.

faqs.question: Is Lucca worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's one of Tuscany's most charming towns, flat and car-free inside the walls, and a calmer base than Florence.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Lucca?
faqs.answer: Two days covers the town. Stay three or four to add Pisa, Florence or the coast.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Lucca?
faqs.answer: April to June and September, around 19 to 28°C.

faqs.question: How do you get to Lucca?
faqs.answer: Fly into Pisa, which has direct flights from the UK, then take the train, about 30 minutes.

faqs.question: Lucca or Pisa?
faqs.answer: Stay in Lucca. It's prettier and more relaxed, and Pisa's tower is an easy half-day trip.
